question.problem:
$\,$ $P(x):$ $0\le x<1$ $\,$ $Q(x):$ $|x|<1$

Consider the predicates $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ above. Which of the following expresses the conditional predicate $P(x)⇒Q(x)?$

- Whenever $|x|<1,$ then $0\le x<1$
- $0\le x<1$ whenever $|x|<1$
- $|x|<1,$ provided that $0\le x<1$
question.worked_solution:
Given that the implication $P⇒Q$ is true, we have the following:

- Whenever $P,$ then $Q$

- $Q$ whenever $P$

- $Q,$ provided that $P$

With that in mind, let's examine the given options.

- Option I reads

$$
\text{Whenever}\,{{|x|<1}_{⏟}}_{Q(x)},\,\text{then}\,{{0\le x<1}_{⏟}}_{P(x)}
$$

which corresponds to $Q(x)⇒P(x).$ $\,\times $

- Option II reads

$$
{{0\le x<1}_{⏟}}_{P(x)}\,\text{whenever}\,{{|x|<1}_{⏟}}_{Q(x)}
$$

which corresponds to $Q(x)⇒P(x).$ $\,\times $

- Option III reads

$$
{{|x|<1\text{,}}_{⏟}}_{Q(x)}\,\text{provided that}\,{{0\le x<1}_{⏟}}_{P(x)}
$$

which corresponds to $P(x)⇒Q(x).$ $\,✓$

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."
